title: Evaluation of Grab's Proposed Acquisition of Trans-Cab for Anti-Competitive Practices
what_it_is: Evaluation of Grab's Proposed Acquisition of Trans-Cab for Anti-Competitive Practices

sections.label: CCCS assesses proposed acquisition impact
sections.summary: CCCS will assess the proposed acquisition's impact on competition and consult relevant stakeholders before deciding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: CCCS will assess the impact of the proposed acquisition on competition and consult relevant stakeholders before reaching a decision on the matter.

sections.label: CCCS two-phase merger review
sections.summary: CCCS uses a two-phase approach, with phase one review expected to be completed within 30 working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CCCS, for the Member's understanding, adopts a two-phase approach in evaluating merger applications that are made through the Competition Commission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And upon receipt of this complete application, CCCS' will carry out a phase one review which involves a quick assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This phase one is expected to be completed within 30 working days.

sections.label: Phase two review and consultation
sections.summary: If phase one raises concerns, CCCS provides key concerns and proceeds to a 120-working-day phase two review, consulting third parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If during the phase one review CCCS is unable to conclude that the merger situation does not raise competition questions or concerns, it will provide the merger parties with a summary of its key concerns and then proceed to carry out a more detailed phase two review, which is expected to take 120 working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To the Member's questions about consultation and concerns, I want to assure him that information provided by third parties play an important role in CCCS' assessment of mergers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CCCS obtains relevant information from third parties, such as competitors and customers, via public consultation and by contacting them directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CCCS, in this case, will be consulting on the proposed acquisition and the public will be able to provide feedback through this public consultation.
